about: The menu-line parameter surface of the Vee plugin format, as data. This file is the documentation surface that docs/scripts/check_params.py holds in agreement with the parser (LineParser.mapParams), the linter (LineParameterKeys.recognized), and each of the three SDKs. Every published parameter table is generated from it by docs/scripts/build_reference.py; do not hand-edit a generated table. Keys are lowercase because LineParser lowercases before dispatching.

groups.title: Text and rendering
groups.blurb: How the row's own text is drawn.

groups.title: Behavior on click
groups.blurb: What happens when a reader activates the row.

groups.title: Placement
groups.blurb: Where the line appears, and where its accessory sits.

groups.title: SF Symbols

groups.title: Annotations
groups.blurb: Small marks attached to a row.

groups.title: Charts and gauges
groups.blurb: The inline accessory slot: a sparkline, a progress bar, or a share chart. See the chart index for the whole matrix.

groups.title: Interactive controls

parameters.summary: Text color — a named color (`red`, `green`, …) or a hex value like `#00ff00`.
Font family name for the text.
Font point size. Clamped to 4–144 points: the value becomes a real font size on a menu row that grows to fit it.
Truncate the displayed text to this many characters.
Trim surrounding whitespace from the text.
Interpret ANSI color escape codes in the text. On by default; set `ansi=false` to disable.
Convert `:shortcode:` tokens (e.g. `:smile:`) into emoji.
Render the text as inline Markdown (bold, italics, etc.).
Render inline `:symbol.name:` tokens in the text as SF Symbols.
Open this URL when the item is clicked.
Run this command on click. Positional args come from `param0`, `param1`, …
Ordered arguments passed to `shell`/`bash`.
parameters.note: An open-ended family matched by prefix rather than enumerated, so it is the one declared exception in the parity check.

parameters.summary: `true` to run the `shell` command in a visible Terminal window; `false` to run it in the background.
Re-run the plugin when the item is clicked.
This line is the Option-key alternate of the line above it.
Render the item greyed-out and non-clickable.
Keyboard shortcut for the item, active while the menu is open.
Run a macOS Shortcut by name when the item is clicked (e.g. `shortcut="Start Meeting"`).
Open a URL in a standalone WebView window, never inside the menu.
Width of the `webview=` window. Bounded by the screen the window opens on — a window wider than the display would put its own close button out of reach.
Height of the `webview=` window. Bounded by the screen the window opens on.
`false` — show the line only in the menu bar, not the dropdown.
Render this line as a real, non-interactive section header instead of a normal item.
Which edge of the row the inline accessory anchors to.
The surfaces this row exists on. A surface not listed omits the row entirely, along with its whole subtree. Supersedes `dropdown=`, which it outranks when both are set.
`false` — no filter query ever matches this row, though it stays visible and clickable while the listing is idle.
Base64-encoded image (or file reference) shown next to the text.
Like `image`, but treated as a template image that adapts to light/dark.
SF Symbol name to show as the item's icon (e.g. `sfimage=cpu`).
Color(s) for the SF Symbol; comma-separated for multicolor symbols.
Point size for the SF Symbol. Clamped to 4–144 points, like `size=`.
SF Symbol configuration as JSON. Example: `sfconfig='{"scale":"large","weight":"bold"}'`.
Hover tooltip text.
Show a checkmark next to the item.
A short badge/chip shown after the text (e.g. `badge=12`).
A comma-separated list of numbers read as a series over time. Renders inline in the menu row; clicking opens a fuller Swift Charts popover.

parameters.appliesTo: progress, sparkline, pie, donut, stackedbar, slider
parameters.summary: Width in points for whichever accessory the row carries, or `full` to stretch it to the row's own width. A row draws at most one accessory, so one parameter sizes any of them. Defaults differ per accessory — see the chart matrix. `full` is refused on `pie=`/`donut=`, which can only fill a width by growing the row. Replaces `progressw=`, `sparklinew=` and `chartw=`. Sizes are clamped: 8–200 points for a chart, 1–200 for a progress bar or sparkline (a bar's own default height is 6).

Height in points for whichever accessory the row carries. Ignored for `toggle=`/`slider=`, whose height is its control size. Replaces `progressh=`, `sparklineh=` and `charth=`. Clamped like `accessoryw=`.
Sparkline width in points, or `full` to stretch it to the row's own width. Clamped to 1–200 points.
Sparkline height in points. Clamped to 1–200 points.
Sparkline line color. Falls back to the row's `color=`, then to the control accent.
Draws a real capsule bar inline in the menu row (e.g. `progress=0.72` or `progress=23.65,100`). Fill uses `color=`.
Bar width in points, or `full` to stretch it to the row's own width. Clamped to 1–200 points.
Bar height in points. Clamped to 1–200 points.
The color of the bar's groove, behind the fill.
The pre-v2 spelling of `progresstrackcolor=`. Still parsed, so published plugins keep working, but the SDKs no longer emit it and `vee lint` warns on it.
Non-negative numbers read as shares of a whole (e.g. `pie=45,30,25`), drawn as a filled circle divided into sectors.
The same shares as `pie=`, drawn with the middle punched out; the hole carries the total.
The same shares as `pie=`, drawn as one horizontal bar whose segments are laid end to end.

The chart's inline width in points, clamped to 8–200. A pie or donut is a circle, so either dimension sizes both. `chartw=full` stretches a `stackedbar=` to the row's own width, and is refused on `pie=`/`donut=` with a diagnostic.
The chart's inline height in points, clamped to 8–200. Defaults to a 24pt circle for `pie=`/`donut=` and 110×12 for `stackedbar=`.
Segment names, positional against the values (e.g. `chartlabels=Docs,Photos,Apps`). Shown in the popover legend and read out by VoiceOver.
Segment colors, positional against the values (e.g. `chartcolors=blue,,orange`). A blank, malformed, or unknown entry keeps that segment's default palette color rather than shifting the rest.
Clicking opens a popover with a switch; flipping it re-invokes the item's `shell=`/`bash=` with the new value.
Clicking opens a popover with a slider; releasing it re-invokes the item's `shell=`/`bash=` with the chosen value (e.g. `slider=0,100,40`).

charts.name: Sparkline

surfaces.widget: node type "sparkline" with "values", or the "trend" template's "trend"

charts.limits: Widget sparkline nodes are truncated at 256 points; non-finite entries are dropped.
charts.popover: Yes — a full Swift Charts line/area chart.
charts.notes: A single value has no series to chart, so it draws as a flat centered baseline; an empty list is ignored entirely.

charts.name: Progress bar
charts.shape: One capsule bar filled to a fraction.

surfaces.widget: "progress" on the card, the "gauge" template's fill

charts.limits: Clamped to 0…1; a non-finite value is dropped.
charts.popover: No — the bar is the whole surface.
charts.notes: Fill takes the row's color=; progresstrackcolor= paints the groove behind it. trackcolor= is the deprecated spelling.

charts.name: Pie
charts.shape: A filled circle divided into sectors.
charts.fullWidth: Not supported — refused with a diagnostic.
charts.limits: 8 segments (the tail folds into 'Other'); size clamped to 8–200 points.
charts.popover: Yes — full size with a labelled legend.
charts.notes: A circle, so accessoryw= or accessoryh= alone sizes both dimensions.

charts.name: Donut
charts.shape: A pie with the middle punched out; the hole carries the total.
charts.fullWidth: Not supported — refused with a diagnostic.
charts.limits: 8 segments (the tail folds into 'Other'); size clamped to 8–200 points.
charts.popover: Yes — full size with a labelled legend.
charts.notes: Same data as pie=; switching between them needs no change to values, labels, or colors.

charts.name: Stacked bar
charts.shape: One horizontal bar whose segments lie end to end.
charts.fullWidth: `accessoryw=full` — the only chart kind that accepts it.
charts.limits: 8 segments (the tail folds into 'Other'); size clamped to 8–200 points.
charts.popover: Yes — full size with a labelled legend.
charts.notes: The only share chart with free width, which is why full applies here and nowhere else.

charts.name: Widget gauge

surfaces.widget: node type "gauge" with "value", or the "gauge" template

charts.fullWidth: Not applicable — a circular gauge takes no size knob.
charts.popover: No — widgets have no popover surface.
charts.notes: Widget-only. The menu bar's nearest equivalent is progress=.
